title: Prompt rewrite safety layer — draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal sketch for a lightweight runtime layer that rewrites incoming prompts to enforce safety and privacy rules before they hit the model. Goal is to have a small, composable service that can be toggled per-route/tenant and returns both the sanitized prompt and a short provenance record suitable for audit logs and downstream evals.

Why this exists (short):
- Many teams want to apply simple sanitization (PII masking, opt-out annotations) and structural normalizations (remove long user signatures, canonicalize timestamps) without changing client code or embedding heavy policy engines in each product.
- We need a standard API for the rewrite pass so rollouts and QA can be done centrally (canary per-tenant, dry-run mode).
- Provide a simple explain endpoint that returns the minimal rationale / rule ids that caused edits so evals can attribute regressions.

Constraints and design principles:
- Latency-sensitive: 1–3 ms P50 additional ideally; must be optional for latency-first routes.
- Deterministic: same input + config => same rewrite.
- Non-destructive: always return an original prompt copy and a rewritten prompt.
- Pluggable rules: rules are small, typed transforms (regex-based, ML-based entity scrubbers, rule-chains).
- Privacy-by-default: any PII removal must be provably one-way (no raw PII persisted).

High-level API shapes (v0):
POST /v0/rewrite
Request JSON:
{
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "route": "string",
  "prompt": "string",
  "modes": ["string"],        // e.g., ["dry-run"] or ["apply", "explain"]
  "config_override": {"string": "string"} // freeform map for per-call adjustments (see config schema)
}
Response JSON:
{
  "original_prompt": "string",
  "rewritten_prompt": "string",
  "applied_rules": ["rule-id-1", "rule-id-2"],
  "provenance": "string",     // compact provenance token (opaque id) for logs
  "explanations": ["human-friendly explanation per rule"],
  "metrics_hint": {"string": "string"} // small key/value for sampling/telemetry
}

POST /v0/explain (optional lighter endpoint)
Request JSON:
{
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "route": "string",
  "prompt": "string",
  "provenance_token": "string?" // if provided, validate/augment explanation
}
Response JSON:
{
  "explanations": ["string"],
  "rule_examples": ["string"],
  "confidence": "float-string"
}

Config schema (runtime):
- config_id: string (versioned)
- rule_chain: ordered list of rule refs (rule-id, params)
- default_mode: apply | dry-run | strip-only
- allowlist/denylist patterns (tenant-scoped)
- pii_policy: low, medium, high (maps to sets of entity scrubbers)
- preserve_context_tokens: boolean (if true, keep token offsets in metadata)
- telemetry_sample_rate: float between 0.0-1.0

Example config snippet (YAML-like for readability):
config_id: rewrite-v2024-08-1
rule_chain:
  - id: redact-ssn
    params: {pattern: "\\\\b\\\\d{3}-\\\\d{2}-\\\\d{4}\\\\b", replacement: "[SSN]"}
  - id: remove-signature
    params: {lines_threshold: 6}
  - id: normalize-dates
    params: {mode: iso}
default_mode: apply
pii_policy: medium
telemetry_sample_rate: 0.02

Rule model (small):
- rule-id: string
- type: regex | ml-ner | custom-js | external-service
- deterministic: true/false
- safe_fallback: what to do if rule errored (skip, dry-run, block)
- human_readable: short explanation text

Runtime architecture (very rough):
[ingress] -> [rewrite-layer (fast-path in-process if simple regexes OR remote service for ML rules)] -> [model-proxy]
   |
   +-> logging: stores {tenant, route, provenance, applied_rules, sampling_decision}

ASCII diagram:
+------------+    +----------------+    +------------+
|  Client    | -> | Rewrite Layer  | -> | Model Gate |
+------------+    +----------------+    +------------+
                       |  ^                 |
                       |  |                 v
                       v  |             (model endpoints)
                 +----------------+
                 | Rule Service   |
                 +----------------+

Notes on fast-path vs heavy path:
- If rule_chain contains only deterministic regex and small heuristics we should run in-thread inside the ingress pod to avoid RPC.
- If rule chain references ml-ner or external classifier, forward to the shared rule-service with a short timeout (50ms) and return dry-run if timeout.

Telemetry and safety signals:
- Counters: rewrites_total, rewrites_applied, rewrites_dryrun, rule_errors, pii_redactions_by_type
- Sampled payload store (keep only tokenized anonymized prompts for debugging).
- Expose a per-tenant slow-query alert if rewrite latency > 25ms p95.

Rollout plan (canary friendly):
- Phase 0: internal dry-run for platform tests; collect applied_rules but do not modify prompt (0% apply).
- Phase 1: opt-in tenants (apply, low pii_policy) and manual QA.
- Phase 2: auto-rollout to new routes with default dry-run, bump telemetry sample rate.
- Phase 3: global apply with SDK switch and per-route overrides.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Provable one-way redaction: what hashing/crypto scheme for provenance token that still allows linking logs to tenant but not reverse PII? encryption with tenant-scoped KMS?
- How to represent composite edits (merge, split) in a compact, replayable diff format?
- UX for customers: a toggle in Console with preview (show rewritten prompt + rule explanations).
- Legal: retention policy on sampled redactions and audit windows. Loop in security/compliance.

Testing checklist (local):
- unit tests for each regex rule with edge-cases and unicode
- property tests for idempotency (rewrite(rewrite(x)) == rewrite(x))
- e2e with upstream model proxies to ensure unchanged tokenization does not cause regressions

Notes-to-self / shorthand traces used during prototyping:
- slack: #platform-rewrite (thread: ts=1692203400)
- proto PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-rewrite-proto/pulls/1
- linear: RW-PR-1327 (privacy redaction scheme)

Small example (realistic):
Request:
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "route": "support-chat:v2",
  "prompt": "Hi, my name is John Doe. My SSN is 123-45-6789. Please reset account.",
  "modes": ["apply", "explain"]
}
Potential response:
{
  "original_prompt": "Hi, my name is John Doe. My SSN is 123-45-6789. Please reset account.",
  "rewritten_prompt": "Hi, my name is [REDACTED]. My SSN is [SSN]. Please reset account.",
  "applied_rules": ["redact-ssn", "mask-name"],
  "explanations": ["SSN pattern matched and replaced", "Detected probable person name and masked per pii_policy=medium"],
  "provenance": "prov:rz-20240815-abc123",
  "metrics_hint": {"sampled_store": "true"}
}

If this looks useful I want to spin up a toy service and bench the fast-path costs. Will follow up with implementation notes and a minimal proto for the rewrite RPC (protobuf + HTTP thin shim).

Quick action items:
- [ ] propose proto in GH (starter PR created)
- [ ] sketch Console preview UI (Jordan / product)
- [ ] sync with Security on retention and KMS patterns
- [ ] prototype regex-in-process vs remote rule-service latency

End of draft.
short_summary: Draft spec for a low-latency prompt rewrite safety layer: API shapes, config schema, runtime decisions, diagrams, rollout plan and test checklist. Personal scratchpad for prototyping.
visibility_note: Personal draft — share with platform-rewrite and security for early feedback
